newsitem.title: JAPAN: Foreign investors seen key to Japan stocks outlook.
newsitem.headline: Foreign investors seen key to Japan stocks outlook.

text.p: Foreign investors are expected to continue to play a key role in the Japanese stock market, where the key index recently hit a new high for this calendar year in volatile trade, brokers said on Wednesday.
Overseas investors bid up shares of export-driven high-technology manufacturers, whose earnings were expected to be bolstered by the yen's weakness against the dollar.
But the recent rally in the yen prompted them to take some quick profits in the blue chips, brokers said.
"Global market watchers are still buying Japanese stocks, which are cheap compared with U.S. stocks that are now in record territory," said a senior broker at a second-tier Japanese securities house.
But some brokers said a further rise in the yen may spark much heavier profit-taking by foreign investors in the Tokyo market.

"If a further yen rise makes foreign investors revise their 1997/98 forecasts for Japanese corporate profits, which are based on 115 yen to the dollar, they could start to take profits again," said a trader at a foreign securities house.

As of Monday, the TOPIX index, a broader index in the Tokyo stock market, had climbed 16.4 percent over the past four weeks, higher than the S&P 500's 11.8 percent gain in New York and the Hong Kong Hang Seng index's 11.4 percent rise, according to data from Credit Lyonnais Securities (Japan).

Foreign investors became net buyers of Japanese stocks in May, with purchases exceeding sales by 109 million shares as of Tuesday. In April, foreign investors were net sellers to the tune of 13 million shares, a European securities house said.

This stance marks a clear contrast to Japanese corporate investors, who were net buyers of 239 million shares in April but switched to net sellers in May. Investment trust funds have been net sellers since April.
